title: Pandemic and Outbreak
description: Use this list to prepare your household for a disease outbreak, school and work closures, and caring for a sick person at home.

sources.title: CDC updates and simplifies respiratory virus recommendations

items.text: At least 2 weeks of shelf-stable food and water, bought a little at a time
Up to a 30-day supply of prescriptions if your insurer allows early refills, and a written medicine list for each person
Thermometer and fever reducers (follow the label; no aspirin for children or teens)
Soap and alcohol-based hand sanitizer with at least 60% alcohol
Well-fitting masks for each person
Oral rehydration salts for vomiting or diarrhea
Know when to call 911: trouble breathing, chest pain, new confusion, cannot stay awake, bluish lips, or no urine for many hours
Stay up to date on flu, COVID-19, and RSV vaccines if eligible, and any vaccine offered for a new outbreak
Household cleaner, disposable gloves, tissues, and trash bags
Pick a sick room (ideally with its own bathroom) and one healthy caregiver
Separate cups, towels, and utensils for a sick person; wash dishes and laundry hot
Portable air purifier or a window fan blowing out to improve ventilation
Arrange backup child care and decide who cares for kids if both parents are sick
Ask your employer about telework and sick leave; check telehealth coverage on your insurance
Line up a neighbor or friend who can drop off groceries or medicine at your door
Know the current stay-home rule: home while sick, back once fever-free 24 hours without medicine and improving, then 5 days of extra care - follow local health department rules in a new outbreak
Never take antibiotics or other prescription drugs not prescribed to you
Follow only official health sources and watch for scams selling fake tests or cures
Save the Disaster Distress Helpline (call or text 1-800-985-5990) for stress and isolation
Books, games, and ways to stay connected by phone or video during long closures
